qs.q: Lobar pneumonia evolves through four stages. What characterizes the "red hepatization" stage?
o: Enzymatic digestion of exudate with macrophage clearance
Vascular congestion with protein-rich fluid and neutrophils
Alveoli packed with neutrophils, red cells, and fibrin
Lysis of red cells with persistent fibrinosuppurative exudate
qs.e: Red hepatization follows congestion and is characterized by liver-like consistency of the lung. Alveolar spaces are packed with neutrophils, red blood cells, and fibrin — giving the red, firm appearance.

qs.q: Which organism most commonly causes community-acquired lobar pneumonia?
qs.e: Streptococcus pneumoniae (pneumococcus) causes more than 90% of lobar pneumonias and is the most common cause of community-acquired acute pneumonia overall.

es.q: Identify the most common lung cancer subtype overall and in non-smokers. Additionally, name the most common bacterial pathogen causing lobar pneumonia.
es.m: Adenocarcinoma is the most common lung cancer subtype overall, and also the most common in women and non-smokers. The most common bacterial pathogen causing lobar pneumonia is *Streptococcus pneumoniae*.
